Thinking about buying?

Everything on this page tells you where prices have been, not where they're going. Nobody can reliably predict whether the market will rise or fall next: not us, and not professional investors. A strong stretch can be followed by a drop, and a bad one by a rally. Averages from past years don't change that.

What history does show: in 15 of the last 20 years (2006–2025), the S&P 500 ended the year higher than it started. But it also fell in about 4 of every 10 months along the way. Ups and downs are normal, even in good years.

That's why many long-term investors don't try to pick the perfect day, month or weekday. They buy a little at a time on a regular schedule, spread their money across many companies (like an S&P 500 index fund), and only invest money they won't need for several years.

This is general education, not advice for your situation. If you're making a real decision, a licensed financial adviser can help.
